The December 2018 FOMC statement reflects a New Keynesian, rule-like response: with unemployment low and output strong, and inflation near the symmetric 2 percent objective, a 25 bp hike and guidance for “some further gradual increases” aim to keep expectations anchored and stabilize Phillips-curve dynamics (Woodford 2003; Galí & Gertler 1999; Christiano, Eichenbaum, and Evans 2005; Svensson on inflation-forecast targeting). The acknowledgment that business fixed investment has moderated is noteworthy in DSGE/RBC settings where investment is a key driver of the business cycle, signaling potential softening even as household spending remains strong. Implementation choices—maintaining the funds rate within 2.25–2.50% via interest on reserves and continuing balance-sheet runoff caps ($30B Treasuries, $20B MBS)—align with the modern floor/corridor operating framework and the literature on central banks setting the policy rate to influence inflation and the output gap. With longer-term inflation expectations little changed and inflation near target, the tone is broadly constructive but slightly hawkish due to the hike and forward guidance, tempered by attention to global/financial developments. Overall, the literature-consistent read is moderately positive but cautious.
